subject: Simple model crashes on Windows, but runs on Linux

messages.author: 461a0c7d7557dffc
messages.subject: Simple model crashes on Windows, but runs on Linux
parts:
Dear INLA crowd,

I came across rather unusual problem. I ran a simple BYM model. Dataset is in the form of 175k observations nested in 3k spatial units, and model is adjusted for two categorical and one continuous variables. There are 46 spatial units with missing observations and I have a row for each of them with missing outcome. 
Everything works as expected here:

f_01 = outcome ~ f(region.struct, 
                        model = "bym", 
                        param = c(prior.iid, prior.besag),  initial = c(initial.iid, initial.besag),
                        graph = "adj/plz_nb.adj") + 
    var1 + var2 + var3

m_01 <- inla(f_01, family="gaussian",
             data = data,
             control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE),
             num.threads = 8)

However when I try to run an ordinary model with no random effects (for comparison):

f_02 = outcome ~ var1 + var2 + var3

m_02 <- inla(f_02, family="gaussian",
             data = data,
             control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE), 
             num.threads = 8)

The INLA crashes on my windows machine:

R version 3.2.3 (2015-12-10)
Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 (64-bit)
Running under: Windows Server 2008 x64 (build 6002) Service Pack 2

INLA version ............: 0.0-1455098891

When I move the dataset and try to run the same thing on my Linux laptop:

R version 3.2.3 (2015-12-10)
Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (64-bit)
Running under: Ubuntu 14.04.4 LTS

INLA version ............: 0.0-1455098891

All works fine.

What might be a reason for such odd behavior? 

Many thanks for help,
radek
